Title: Our [Nitrogen] Fertilized World
Content: It is the engine of agriculture, the key to plenty in our crowded, hungry world. …

…Enter modern chemistry. Giant factories capture inert nitrogen gas from the vast stores in our atmosphere and force it into a chemical union with the hydrogen in natural gas, creating the reactive compounds that plants crave. That nitrogen fertilizer – more than a `text(hundred million tons)` applied worldwide `text(every year)` – fuels bountiful harvests. Without it, human civilization in its current form could not exist. Our planet’s soil simply could not grow enough food to provide all `text(seven billion)` of us our accustomed diet. In fact, almost `text(half)` of the nitrogen found in our bodies’ muscle and organ tissue started out in a fertilizer factory.
